title: Chemistry: Acid, base and salt (Past Year Questions)

questions.q_en: Why does the milkman add a very small amount of baking soda to fresh milk?
options_en: To reduce the pH of the fresh milk from 6 to slightly more acidic
To increase the pH of the fresh milk from 6 to slightly alkaline
To maintain the pH of the fresh milk at 6 for a longer time
To reduce the pH of the fresh milk from 6 to slightly alkaline
questions.solution_en:
· Fresh milk is slightly acidic (pH ~6).

· Adding baking soda (NaHCO₃) makes it slightly alkaline, preventing it from turning sour quickly due to lactic acid formation.

questions.q_en: Select the synthetic indicator from among the given options.
questions.solution_en:
· Methyl orange is a synthetic indicator, meaning it is artificially prepared in laboratories. It is commonly used in acid-base titrations.

· It turns red in acidic solutions and yellow in basic solutions.

Further Insight:

· Turmeric - Natural indicator (from the turmeric plant).

· Cabbage juice - Natural indicator (from red cabbage).

· Litmus solution - Derived from lichens, so it's a natural indicator.

questions.q_en: Which of the following is the compound with the chemical formula H₂SO₄?
questions.solution_en:
· H₂SO₄: The chemical formula for Sulfuric Acid, a strong mineral acid with the structure H₂SO₄ (two hydrogens, one sulfur, four oxygens).

· Other Options:

o Nitric Acid: HNO₃, used in fertilizers and explosives.

o Sulfurous Acid: H₂SO₃, a weaker acid formed from sulfur dioxide.

o Hydrogen Sulfide: H₂S, a toxic gas, not an acid in this context.

Further Insights:

· Industrial Uses: Sulfuric acid is a "king of chemicals," used in batteries, fertilizers (e.g., ammonium sulfate), and chemical synthesis.

· Properties: Highly corrosive, it dehydrates substances and is a strong dehydrating agent (e.g., chars sugar).

· Safety: Handling H₂SO₄ requires precautions due to its reactivity, a key topic in chemistry education.

questions.q_en: What are bases that are soluble in water called?
questions.solution_en:
Bases that are soluble in water are called Alkalis. When dissolved in water, alkalis produce hydroxide ions (OH⁻). All alkalis are bases, but not all bases are alkalis (some bases are insoluble in water).

Explanation of Other Options:

• Alkenes: These are unsaturated hydrocarbons containing at least one carbon-carbon double bond. They are organic compounds, not related to the definition of water-soluble bases.

• Acids: Acids are substances that produce hydrogen ions (H⁺) or hydronium ions (H₃O⁺) when dissolved in water, or are proton donors. They are the chemical opposites of bases.

• Alkanes: These are saturated hydrocarbons consisting only of hydrogen and carbon atoms and all bonds are single bonds. They are organic compounds.

Further insights:

• Examples of alkalis include sodium hydroxide (NaOH), potassium hydroxide (KOH), and calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)₂ - sparingly soluble).

• Alkalis typically have a bitter taste and feel soapy to the touch (due to saponification of fats on the skin).

• They turn red litmus paper blue and react with acids to form salt and water (neutralization).

questions.q_en: Acid changes the colour of blue litmus to _________
questions.solution_en:
Acid turns blue litmus red. Bases turn red litmus blue.

Special type of substances are used to test whether a substance is acidic or basic. These substances are known as indicators. The indicators change their colour when added to a solution containing an acidic or a basic substance. Turmeric, litmus, china rose petals (Gudhal), etc., are some of the naturally occurring indicators.

questions.q_en: Which theory, independently introduced in 1923, led to the concept of acid-base conjugate pairs?
questions.solution_en:
• A Brønsted-Lowry acid is a substance that can donate a proton (H⁺), and a Brønsted-Lowry base is a substance that can accept a proton

• A Lewis acid is a substance that can accept an electron pair, while a Lewis base is a substance that can donate an electron pair.

• An Arrhenius acid is a substance that increases the concentration of hydrogen ions (H⁺) in aqueous solution, while an Arrhenius base increases the concentration of hydroxide ions (OH⁻).​

• Sir Humphry Davy proposed that acids are substances that contain replaceable hydrogen atoms, and their acidic properties are due to the presence of hydrogen.​

questions.q_en: Acidic drain cleaners made of ______ or ______ acid are powerful enough to clear heavy-duty hair, food, grease, soap scum or paper-based clogs in 15 minutes or less.
questions.solution_en: Acidic drain openers are made with hydrochloric or sulfuric acids. This type of drain opener is best for grease clogs, heavy-duty hair build-up, organic waste, soap scum, or tough clogs in a shower or kitchen sink. Their effectiveness to dissolve clogs is almost unmatched due to their chemical makeup. They are best used on newer pipes in a home or commercial setting, as the strength of this cleaner may damage older pipes. Users should wear protective gear while using this opener.

questions.q_en: The Ph of a neutral solution is _____ .
questions.solution_en: A pH of 7 indicates a neutral solution, a pH greater than 7 indicates a basic solution, and a pH of less than 7 indicates an acidic solution.
questions.solution_hi: A pH of 7 indicates a neutral solution, a pH greater than 7 indicates a basic solution, and a pH of less than 7 indicates an acidic solution.
